data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR package with a clean PKGBUILD that downloads from the official upstream GitHub repository with a pinned version and valid SHA512 checksum. The package() function only performs standard installation of the executable and man page. No dangerous top-level code, network operations, or suspicious constructs are present. The disagreement between reports was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b model, not by a genuine security concern. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully completed the review and found no issues, and the initial PKGBUILD audit in the qwen model also found no dangerous top-level code before the API error occurred.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen3-235b model when attempting to review the PKGBUILD, not by differing security assessments. The model's initial audit of the PKGBUILD succeeded and found it safe, but the full review failed due to an API error. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed both files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b model failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to HTTP 400 API error
learnings: When a report ends in a tool error (API failure, timeout, etc.), it should be treated as missing data and excluded from disagreement calculations rather than contributing to an 'inconclusive' verdict
The audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms when encountering API errors to prevent incomplete reviews
Initial PKGBUILD audits (for top-level code) that succeed should be preserved and weighted appropriately even if subsequent full reviews fail
